quizName: DMV Practice Test #15 20 Questions • Passing Score 15

questions.question: A helmet will give you the most protection if it is all of the following, except:

options.text: Approved by the U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT).
Loose-fitting.
Free of defects.

questions.correctAnswerText: Loose-fitting.
questions.explanation: A helmet protects you best when it meets U.S. DOT standards, fits snugly all around your head, and has no defects like cracks, loose padding, or frayed straps.

questions.question: A main cause of single-vehicle motorcycle crashes is:

options.text: Riding too fast for weather conditions.
Turning too wide in a curve.
Running off the road while trying to avoid another vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turning too wide in a curve.
questions.explanation: A main cause of single-vehicle crashes is turning too wide in a curve. Turning too wide can cause your motorcycle to leave the road or hit an object.

questions.question: If your rear wheel locks up while stopping on a road with good traction, you should:

options.text: Keep the wheel locked until you stop completely.
Release the rear brake and use only the front brake.
Release the rear brake and quickly apply it again.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the wheel locked until you stop completely.
questions.explanation: If your rear wheel locks while stopping on a road with good traction, you can keep it locked until you stop. You can still control your motorcycle as long as it stays upright and travels in a straight line.

questions.question: Smaller vehicles appear to be ________ and slower than they really are.

options.text: Closer
Farther away
Larger

questions.correctAnswerText: Farther away
questions.explanation: It is hard to judge the speed and distance of a small vehicle like a motorcycle. Do not assume that larger vehicle drivers will accurately judge your speed and location.

questions.question: When approaching a blind intersection, you should:

options.text: Move into the part of your lane that makes other drivers see you as early as possible.
Stop at the sign or signal and proceed normally.
Flash your lights and honk your horn to alert other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move into the part of your lane that makes other drivers see you as early as possible.
questions.explanation: When approaching a blind intersection, move into the part of your lane that allows other drivers to see you as early as possible.

questions.question: You should keep a larger following distance:

options.text: If the road is slippery.
If traffic is light.
If you can see past the vehicles in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: If the road is slippery.
questions.explanation: You need more space if your motorcycle will take longer to stop. If the road is slippery, if you cannot see past the vehicle ahead, or if traffic is heavy, increase your following distance to at least four seconds.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Yield
Slow-moving vehicle
Railroad crossing

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow-moving vehicle
questions.explanation: This sign is placed on the back of slow-moving vehicles that travel slower than 25 mph, such as farm equipment, construction vehicles, or horse-drawn wagons.

questions.question: When looking through a turn, you should:

options.text: Turn just your head, not your shoulders.
Turn your head and shoulders to see better.
Turn your shoulders, but not your head.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn just your head, not your shoulders.
questions.explanation: When taking a turn, look toward where you want to go. Turn only your head, keep your shoulders still, and keep your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: _________ of motorcycle and car crashes are caused by car drivers failing to give the right-of-way to motorcyclists.

options.text: One-quarter
More than half
One-half

questions.correctAnswerText: More than half
questions.explanation: More than half of motorcycle and car crashes happen because car drivers fail to give the right-of-way to motorcyclists. Never assume that larger vehicle drivers will yield the right-of-way, even if they are required to do so.

questions.question: Where should you position your motorcycle when entering a curve?

options.text: On the outside of the curve
On the inside of the curve
Wherever traffic and road conditions require

questions.correctAnswerText: Wherever traffic and road conditions require
questions.explanation: Every curve is different. When turning, choose a lane position that fits the conditions and adjust as needed.

questions.question: What does a solid yellow traffic light mean?

options.text: The red light is coming next.
The green light is coming next.
Stop and wait for traffic to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: The red light is coming next.
questions.explanation: A yellow light warns you that the light will turn red soon. Slow down and stop before the intersection if you can do so safely. If you are already in the intersection, continue through.

questions.question: Before starting a turn, a motorcyclist should change gears to:

options.text: Keep the engine power steady through the turn.
Keep both hands on the handlebars during the turn.
Keep the motorcycle from slowing down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the engine power steady through the turn.
questions.explanation: Change gears before you turn. Shifting gears while turning can cause sudden power changes to the rear wheel and make the motorcycle skid. If you must shift while turning, do it smoothly.

questions.question: A person with a blood alcohol content (BAC) of ____ or higher is considered intoxicated.

options.text: 0.02 percent
0.04 percent
0.08 percent

questions.correctAnswerText: 0.08 percent
questions.explanation: In Virginia, a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher means you are intoxicated. An intoxicated person cannot legally drive.

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: The front brake is stronger than the rear brake.
The rear brake is stronger than the front brake.
Both brakes are equally strong.

questions.correctAnswerText: The front brake is stronger than the rear brake.
questions.explanation: The front brake is stronger than the rear brake. It provides at least 70 percent of a motorcycle's stopping power.

questions.question: When riding behind another vehicle, you should position yourself:

options.text: So the driver can see you in the side mirror.
So the driver can see you in the rearview mirror.
So the driver can see you through the passenger window.

questions.correctAnswerText: So the driver can see you in the rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Follow the car in the center of your lane. This position puts you in the driver's rearview mirror, where drivers look most often.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Stop.
Yield to other drivers.
A stop sign is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A stop sign is ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They tell you about road conditions ahead. This sign warns that a stop sign is coming.

questions.question: When passing a vehicle, you:

options.text: Can go 10 mph over the speed limit.
Cannot exceed the speed limit.
Must go faster than the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cannot exceed the speed limit.
questions.explanation: Always obey the speed limit when passing. Only pass where it is safe and legal.

questions.question: When motorcyclists ride in a group:

options.text: Inexperienced riders should be in front.
Inexperienced riders should be near the front.
Inexperienced riders should be in back.

questions.correctAnswerText: Inexperienced riders should be near the front.
questions.explanation: Put less experienced riders near the front, behind the leader. This lets experienced riders lead and watch the newer riders.

questions.question: If you will carry a passenger on your motorcycle, you likely need to:

options.text: Lower the tire pressure.
Make no tire pressure changes.
Raise the tire pressure.

questions.correctAnswerText: Raise the tire pressure.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight to your motorcycle. Add a few pounds of pressure to your tires before riding. Check your owner's manual for the correct pressure.

questions.question: When making a U-turn:

options.text: Use both brakes at the same time.
Do not use the front brake because it could tip the bike over.
Use the front brake to keep the bike stable.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not use the front brake because it could tip the bike over.
questions.explanation: Do not use the front brake during a U-turn because it could cause the bike to tip. Use the rear brake instead to control your speed.
